questions.q: Tell me about your back-office or operations work. What processes did you handle, in which tools, and with what daily targets?
questions.looks_for: Real processes (order processing, documentation, reports, verification, MIS), tools used, daily volume and targets, and their own part.

questions.q: Describe a time you improved a process or caught a problem early. What did you notice and what happened after?
questions.looks_for: Specific observation, action taken (checklist, sheet, raising alert), and a clear result like fewer errors or time saved.

questions.q: What is a TAT or SLA in operations, and why does missing it matter?
questions.looks_for: Agreed turnaround time or service level; missing it hurts customers, penalties, trust; explains tracking and early escalation.

questions.q: How do you keep track of many pending tasks so nothing is missed at the end of the day?
questions.looks_for: Uses a tracker or sheet, priorities by deadline, daily checks, notes handover, updates status honestly.

questions.q: Why are checklists and maker-checker steps used in back-office work?
questions.looks_for: Reduce errors, one person makes, another checks; especially for money or customer data; builds accountability.

questions.q: Near the end of the day you see that 40 orders were processed with a wrong address field because of a sheet error. What would you do?
questions.looks_for: Stops further processing, tells the supervisor at once, lists affected orders, fixes the source, corrects records, and helps prevent repeat.

questions.q: Why do you want this operations and back-office job, when can you join (state your notice period), and what salary do you expect?
questions.looks_for: Clear reason linked to the work, states notice period or joining date in days or weeks, and gives an expected monthly or yearly salary figure or range without dodging.
